title: PANDA-D: Interface-free determination of two dynamic contact angles
authors: Georgii K. Vandyshev, Grigorii S. Gorkaev, Nikolay D. Kondratyuk, Kirill M. Gerke, Ilia V. Kopanichuk
abstract: Contact angles are central descriptors of wetting and capillary behavior at solid--fluid interfaces. Dynamic contact angles in molecular simulations are commonly extracted from two-dimensional liquid--vapor contours and near-wall tangent fits. We introduce PANDA-D, an extension of Predicting Angle from Nanoscale Density Analysis (PANDA) that determines both contact angles of a driven liquid roll without extracting an interface. The density profile measures occupied layer width but does not identify which meniscus is advancing. The method resolves this ambiguity by jointly fitting density and the layerwise center-of-mass displacement relative to the roll. A circular-meniscus model maps these profiles to receding and advancing angles and an effective near-wall offset. On synthetic rolls with prescribed angles, the reconstruction error is $0.29^\circ$ root-mean-square. We then analyze force-driven Lennard--Jones rolls between crystalline walls. Joint fits reproduce both measured profiles, whereas density-only fits can match density while assigning incorrect asymmetry. The resulting angles agree with independently determined circle-fit angles to $0.84^\circ$ root-mean-square. Across four wall--fluid attractions, the receding angle decreases and the advancing angle increases with force, approximately linearly over the studied ranges. By eliminating contour thresholds and near-wall tangent extrapolation from the primary estimate, the two-profile approach enables reproducible, automated angle analysis across molecular trajectories.
summary: This paper introduces PANDA-D, a novel computational method to determine dynamic contact angles in molecular simulations by jointly fitting density and layerwise center-of-mass displacement profiles. It overcomes the ambiguity of traditional interface detection by using two correlated observables. The method proves highly accurate and robust, providing a reproducible tool for analyzing wetting behavior under external forces.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately determining dynamic contact angles ($	heta_{adv}$ and $	heta_{rec}$) at solid-fluid interfaces in molecular simulations without relying on ambiguous 2D interface contour extraction.
main_result: The proposed PANDA-D method successfully determines both dynamic contact angles by jointly fitting density and layerwise center-of-mass displacement profiles, achieving agreement with independent measurements within $0.84^\circ$ RMSE.
method: PANDA-D extends the PANDA method by performing a joint fit of two observables—the density profile and the layerwise center-of-mass displacement—to a geometric model based on circular menisci.
model_or_system: The study models a liquid bridge (roll) spanning a slit between crystalline solid walls, simulated using Molecular Dynamics with a Lennard-Jones potential. The analysis focuses on non-equilibrium wetting phenomena driven by external forces.
key_observables: Dynamic contact angles ($	heta_{adv}, 	heta_{rec}$), density profile, layerwise center-of-mass displacement profile, and the dependence of angles on applied external force ($F_{ext}$).
important_parameters: Wall-fluid attraction strength ($\epsilon^*_{sf}$), applied external force ($F_{ext}$), and the pore height ($H$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the menisci can be accurately mapped to circular arcs via a geometric forward model, and that the joint fit of density and displacement resolves the ambiguity inherent in density-only analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate molecular configurations of liquid rolls (equilibrium and force-driven), compare synthetic angle recoveries, and plot the dependence of receding and advancing angles on applied force, comparing results to independent circle-fit estimates.
paper_structure: The paper introduces PANDA-D by first validating it on synthetic rolls, then applying it to force-driven Lennard-Jones rolls, demonstrating the superiority of the joint density/displacement fit over density-only fits, and finally analyzing the linear force dependence of the resulting angles.
why_interesting: While focused on fluid dynamics, the rigorous application of joint profile fitting to resolve an ill-posed inverse problem (identifying advancing vs. receding menisci) shares methodological parallels with reconstructing complex quantum states or dynamics from limited, correlated measurements.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Molecular configurations of the slit-spanning liquid roll at ϵ∗ sf = 0.35: (a) an equilibrium configuration and (b) a force-driven configuration. The plotted coordinates x and z are normalized by the pore height H, with z = 0 at the pore center. Blue particles are fluid and gray particles are the fixed walls. In (b), the receding and advancing meniscus arcs and angle markers are red and orange, respectively. The imposed force points along +x. These schematic overlays are not the contour used by PANDA-D.

Figure 2: Synthetic validation of PANDA-D at three equilibrium angles and three filling fractions. Prescribed receding and advancing angles are compared with those reconstructed from particle-derived density and center-of-mass profiles. The diagonal denotes exact recovery; the complete set contains 45 roll geometries and 90 individual angles.

Figure 3: Equilibrium PANDA-α contact angle for the well-sampled ϵff = 1 series. Only the six long-run ϵ∗ sf = ϵsf/ϵff points are shown; the two inserted interaction strengths, 0.315 and 0.385, each have duplicate trajectories. Error bars are temporal-block standard deviations. The black straight line is an unweighted linear least-squares fit of the means, not a physical theory.

Figure 4: Example MD profiles and fits: (a) normalized density and (b) normalized layerwise center-of-mass displace- ment. The plotted wall-normal coordinate z is normalized by H. Black curves are measured time averages, gray bands represent temporal scatter, green dashed curves use density alone, and red dash-dotted curves use both profiles. The density-only solution fits panel (a) but misses the asymmetry measured in panel (b). Dotted vertical lines mark the wall positions; plotted zero extensions outside populated bins do not imply measured q = 0 in empty bins.

Figure 5: PANDA-family estimates versus independent circle-fit contact angles. (a) Historical density-only control with an older equilibrium reference; (b) refreshed density-plus-center-of-mass PANDA-D estimate with the corrected same-mode reference. The dashed line is equality. Different accepted sample sizes and reference conventions make the panels illustrative rather than a controlled ablation.
